questions.stem: This cross-sectional illustration of an arterial wall labels several concentric layers. Which structural feature primarily allows a large elastic artery to expand during systole and recoil during diastole?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The adventitial connective tissue sheath alone

choices.label: B
choices.text: A single layer of endothelial cells lining the lumen

choices.label: C
choices.text: Rigid collagen fibers that resist any deformation

choices.label: D
choices.text: Valves within the vessel wall directing flow

choices.label: E
choices.text: Elastic membranes and elastin fibers within the wall

explanation.summary: The internal and external elastic membranes and abundant elastin allow large arteries to stretch as blood is ejected in systole and recoil in diastole, sustaining pressure between beats; collagen provides tensile strength and smooth muscle adjusts tone, but elastic tissue drives the reversible expansion.
explanation.whyCorrect: The internal and external elastic membranes and abundant elastin allow large arteries to stretch as blood is ejected in systole and recoil in diastole, sustaining pressure between beats; collagen provides tensile strength and smooth muscle adjusts tone, but elastic tissue drives the reversible expansion.

questions.stem: This histologic section places a femoral artery beside a femoral vein at the same magnification. What accounts for the artery having a much thicker, rounder wall than the adjacent vein?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Higher pressure and wall tension require more elastin and collagen for structural support

choices.label: B
choices.text: The artery carries a larger blood volume than the vein

choices.label: C
choices.text: Arterial blood viscosity erodes the venous wall over time

choices.label: D
choices.text: The vein is filled with valves that thin its wall

choices.label: E
choices.text: The artery has a smaller radius, demanding a thicker wall

explanation.summary: Arteries are exposed to high pressures and large radii, so by the law of Laplace they experience high wall tension and require thick walls rich in elastin and collagen; veins operate at low pressure and thus have thin, less muscular walls, giving the collapsed, thin-walled appearance seen here.
explanation.whyCorrect: Arteries are exposed to high pressures and large radii, so by the law of Laplace they experience high wall tension and require thick walls rich in elastin and collagen; veins operate at low pressure and thus have thin, less muscular walls, giving the collapsed, thin-walled appearance seen here.

questions.stem: This figure compares three capillary wall structures. Which type is found in organs such as the liver and bone marrow and is the most permeable, allowing passage of plasma proteins and cells?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Tight-junction capillary of the blood-brain barrier

explanation.summary: Discontinuous (sinusoidal) capillaries have large gaps in their wall, making them highly permeable; they are found where large substances and cells must cross, such as liver, spleen, and bone marrow.
explanation.whyCorrect: Discontinuous (sinusoidal) capillaries have large gaps in their wall, making them highly permeable; they are found where large substances and cells must cross, such as liver, spleen, and bone marrow.

questions.stem: This H&E light-microscopy field of a vessel wall shows a wavy line separating two of the concentric layers. What does that undulating boundary represent?

choices.label: B
choices.text: The basement membrane of the endothelium

choices.label: D
choices.text: A layer of fibrin from early clotting

explanation.summary: The prominent wavy line between the tunica intima and tunica media is the internal elastic lamina, a sheet of elastic tissue that appears crimped in fixed sections.
explanation.whyCorrect: The prominent wavy line between the tunica intima and tunica media is the internal elastic lamina, a sheet of elastic tissue that appears crimped in fixed sections.

questions.stem: This is a histologic section through the wall of the aorta. What histologic feature of the tunica media allows this vessel to expand during systole and recoil during diastole?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A thick layer of skeletal muscle

choices.label: B
choices.text: A single layer of smooth muscle

choices.label: E
choices.text: A high density of elastin fibers

explanation.summary: The aorta is an elastic artery whose tunica media is packed with elastin, letting it stretch under the systolic surge and recoil during diastole to smooth blood flow.
explanation.whyCorrect: The aorta is an elastic artery whose tunica media is packed with elastin, letting it stretch under the systolic surge and recoil during diastole to smooth blood flow.

questions.stem: This specially stained section of aortic tunica media highlights dark, wavy bands running across the field. What component is this stain selectively demonstrating?

explanation.summary: An elastin (elastic) stain darkens the dense, wavy elastic lamellae of the aortic media, illustrating the high elastin content characteristic of elastic arteries.
explanation.whyCorrect: An elastin (elastic) stain darkens the dense, wavy elastic lamellae of the aortic media, illustrating the high elastin content characteristic of elastic arteries.

questions.stem: This histologic field shows two adjacent small vessels, the smaller labeled and the slightly larger companion nearby. Which feature typically distinguishes the smallest artery shown from an accompanying vein of similar size?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is filled with lymph rather than blood

choices.label: C
choices.text: It has a relatively thicker wall and often an incomplete internal elastic lamina

choices.label: E
choices.text: It has the thickest adventitia of any vessel

explanation.summary: Arterioles are the smallest arteries; they have proportionally thicker muscular walls than the thin-walled venules, though they lack an external elastic lamina and often have an incomplete internal elastic lamina.
explanation.whyCorrect: Arterioles are the smallest arteries; they have proportionally thicker muscular walls than the thin-walled venules, though they lack an external elastic lamina and often have an incomplete internal elastic lamina.

questions.stem: This electron micrograph shows a capillary whose endothelial cells are interrupted by tiny pores while the basement membrane remains intact. In which tissue would you most expect to find this capillary type?

explanation.summary: Fenestrated capillaries have pores (fenestrae) in the endothelium over an intact basement membrane, allowing greater transit of fluid and molecules; they populate the glomeruli, intestines, and endocrine glands.
explanation.whyCorrect: Fenestrated capillaries have pores (fenestrae) in the endothelium over an intact basement membrane, allowing greater transit of fluid and molecules; they populate the glomeruli, intestines, and endocrine glands.

questions.stem: This H&E section of an artery from an elderly patient shows dense inflammation with multinucleated cells extending across the vessel wall and a markedly narrowed lumen. This inflammatory process most classically involves which portion of the vessel wall?

explanation.summary: The classic histologic picture of giant cell arteritis is a transmural inflammatory infiltrate of lymphocytes and macrophages with multinucleated giant cells involving all layers of the wall, producing intimal thickening and luminal narrowing. Isolated single-layer involvement is not characteristic.
explanation.whyCorrect: The classic histologic picture of giant cell arteritis is a transmural inflammatory infiltrate of lymphocytes and macrophages with multinucleated giant cells involving all layers of the wall, producing intimal thickening and luminal narrowing. Isolated single-layer involvement is not characteristic.

questions.stem: This histologic section of a mitral valve leaflet shows an irregularly thickened, expanded middle layer between the fibrosa and atrialis. This degenerative change is the underlying cause of which condition?

explanation.summary: Myxomatous degeneration expands the spongiosa with proteoglycans, weakening the leaflet and chordae so the valve becomes floppy and bulges into the LA during systole (mitral valve prolapse).
explanation.whyCorrect: Myxomatous degeneration expands the spongiosa with proteoglycans, weakening the leaflet and chordae so the valve becomes floppy and bulges into the LA during systole (mitral valve prolapse).

questions.stem: This myocardial histology field shows an inflammatory infiltrate among the cardiac muscle fibers. This lymphocytic pattern is most characteristic of which etiology of myocarditis?

explanation.summary: A predominantly lymphocytic infiltrate is characteristic of viral myocarditis; bacterial infection tends to produce neutrophilic infiltrates and hypersensitivity reactions produce eosinophilic infiltrates.
explanation.whyCorrect: A predominantly lymphocytic infiltrate is characteristic of viral myocarditis; bacterial infection tends to produce neutrophilic infiltrates and hypersensitivity reactions produce eosinophilic infiltrates.

questions.stem: This histologic section of a mitral leaflet shows an irregularly expanded middle (spongiosa) layer filled with loose myxoid matrix. This finding is the hallmark of which valve disorder?

explanation.summary: Accumulation of proteoglycan-rich myxoid material expanding the spongiosa and disrupting the fibrosa weakens the leaflet, producing the redundant, floppy valve of myxomatous degeneration and mitral valve prolapse.
explanation.whyCorrect: Accumulation of proteoglycan-rich myxoid material expanding the spongiosa and disrupting the fibrosa weakens the leaflet, producing the redundant, floppy valve of myxomatous degeneration and mitral valve prolapse.

questions.stem: This histologic section shows normal pericardium overlying heart. The deeply eosinophilic tissue at the bottom of the field is composed primarily of which cell type?

explanation.summary: The myocardium seen at the base of the section is made of cardiomyocytes, beneath the visceral pericardium and its overlying adipose tissue.
explanation.whyCorrect: The myocardium seen at the base of the section is made of cardiomyocytes, beneath the visceral pericardium and its overlying adipose tissue.

questions.stem: This histologic field of pericardial fluid is dominated by inflammatory cells with multilobed nuclei. This dense infiltrate indicates that the pericarditis is most likely due to what?

explanation.summary: A neutrophil-rich (purulent) infiltrate is the hallmark of bacterial pericarditis, distinguishing it from the lymphocyte-predominant serous inflammation of viral causes.
explanation.whyCorrect: A neutrophil-rich (purulent) infiltrate is the hallmark of bacterial pericarditis, distinguishing it from the lymphocyte-predominant serous inflammation of viral causes.

questions.stem: This developmental sequence depicts formation of the interatrial septum. The flap-valve opening present in the final panel closes after birth and leaves which adult structure?

explanation.summary: The foramen ovale, bounded by septum primum and septum secundum, permits fetal right-to-left flow. When left atrial pressure rises after birth it seals, leaving the fossa ovalis as a depression in the adult atrial septum.
explanation.whyCorrect: The foramen ovale, bounded by septum primum and septum secundum, permits fetal right-to-left flow. When left atrial pressure rises after birth it seals, leaving the fossa ovalis as a depression in the adult atrial septum.
